name: English welted dress shoe
summary: The lace-up dress shoe of the English gentleman. It is a closed-lacing Oxford or an open-lacing Derby in polished calf, sewn to a leather sole with a welt that a cobbler can replace.

philosophy.core_thesis: A dress shoe lasts decades when its sole is welted and the upper is fine calf, so the shoe is a quiet sign of care.
design_principles: Stitch the leather sole to the upper through a welt, so that a cobbler can resole it four to six times.
Close the throat of an Oxford with a lace tab that is sewn under the vamp.
Keep the toe round or slightly chiselled, and the toe cap plain.
Cut the heel stack at 2.5 cm and the waist of the sole narrow and close.
Burnish the toe and the heel to a dark shine in two coats of polish.
Use 5 to 6 pairs of eyelets, with a flat waxed lace.
Choose a last with a quiet shape: no sharp toe, no square toe.
anti_patterns: A glued rubber sole on a dress shoe
Decorative buckles and chains on a business shoe
Chrome tanned leather with a plastic shine

silhouette.shape: A long, low shoe with a round, slightly chiselled toe and a waisted sole.
silhouette.line: One clean line from the toe cap along the vamp to the lace, with a low arch.
silhouette.fit: Close at the heel and the instep; the lace tightens the quarters around the foot.
silhouette.proportion: Heel 2.5 cm; vamp length about 40 percent of the shoe; five or six eyelet pairs.
rules: Hold the line plain: a toe cap or a wing tip, but not both.
Stitch the welt at the edge of the sole in fine, even stitches.
Match the belt to the shoe in colour and finish.
Wear black for the city, brown for the country.

fabrics.rule: Use calfskin for the upper, vegetable-tanned leather for the sole and the welt, and shell cordovan or suede as the luxury and country choices.

methods: Goodyear welt stitched around the insole rib
hand lasting over a wooden last
leather and cork filler under the insole
construction.closures: Flat waxed laces through five or six pairs of eyelets; closed lacing for an Oxford, open lacing for a Derby.
construction.details: A straight toe cap, a perforated medallion on a brogue, a leather-lined heel, a stacked leather heel with a rubber top piece.

surface.pattern: Plain, or fine perforations (brogueing) along the seams on a country shoe.
surface.gloss: Polished calf at 30–60 GU; suede at 2–5 GU; patent for evening at 80–95 GU.
surface.wear: The style wants a patina: the leather darkens, creases at the flex and takes a deeper shine each year.

palette.strategy: Black for town, a range of browns for the country, and one plain oxblood.

processes: hand cutting and closing the upper
making.scale: Bespoke from a last carved for each client (about 40 hours) or factory made in Northampton, with 200 steps for each pair.
making.signs: A clean welt stitch, an even edge finish, and a shape that holds after years of wear.

pieces.form: Closed-lacing Oxford with a straight toe cap
Open-lacing Derby with a full brogue pattern
Penny loafer with a saddle strap on a welted sole
Plain evening Oxford in patent leather
Chelsea boot with elastic side panels

emotion.target_response: A feeling of quiet trust: an old, careful craft that does not need to show off.

use_cases: a brief for a tailored menswear shoe
a still-life prompt for a leather shoe
a care guide for a resolable shoe
avoid_when: the brief wants a sports shoe
the brief wants a fashion heel
the brief wants a glued, cheap shoe

modifiers.how: Thicken the sole, raise the shaft to the ankle, and add a yellow welt stitch.
Replace the leather with canvas and the welted sole with a vulcanised rubber sole.

ornament_level.note: Brogueing and a medallion are the only ornament of a dress shoe.
